from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'One location can be described by different coordinate systems.',
            'The drone follows a grid aligned with the streets.',
            'The bird sees the world through a tilted grid.',
            'Both observers point to the same physical location.',
            'Same spot, but different coordinates based on their perspective.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of 'Perspective'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        GRAY_COLOR = "#555555"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Grid area reference
        grid_area_tl = "A1"
        grid_area_br = "F6"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        drone_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GRAY_COLOR, "stroke_width": 2},
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "stroke_color": GRAY_COLOR}
        ).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(drone_grid, grid_area_tl, grid_area_br)
        
        drone_asset = SVGMobject("/mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg")
        drone_asset.scale(0.2)
        # Position the drone at (3, 2) relative to the drone_grid
        drone_asset.move_to(drone_grid.c2p(3, 2))
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeIn(drone_grid),
            FadeIn(drone_asset)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        drone_arrow = Arrow(
            start=drone_grid.get_origin(),
            end=drone_asset.get_center(),
            buff=0,
            color=BLUE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        drone_label = Text("Drone: [3, 2]", font_size=20, color=BLUE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(drone_label, "B6")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY_COLOR),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR),
            Create(drone_arrow),
            FadeIn(drone_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        bird_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": YELLOW_COLOR, "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "stroke_color": YELLOW_COLOR}
        ).scale(0.6).rotate(30 * DEGREES)
        self.place_in_area(bird_grid, grid_area_tl, grid_area_br)
        
        bird_origin_marker = Triangle(color=YELLOW_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.12).move_to(drone_grid.get_origin())
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY_COLOR),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR),
            FadeIn(bird_grid),
            FadeIn(bird_origin_marker)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Bird coordinates calculation: (3, 2) rotated by -30 degrees
        # x' = 3*cos(30) + 2*sin(30) = 3*0.866 + 2*0.5 = 2.598 + 1 = 3.598
        # y' = -3*sin(30) + 2*cos(30) = -3*0.5 + 2*0.866 = -1.5 + 1.732 = 0.232
        bird_arrow = Arrow(
            start=bird_grid.get_origin(),
            end=drone_asset.get_center(),
            buff=0,
            color=YELLOW_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        bird_label = Text("Bird: [3.60, 0.23]", font_size=20, color=YELLOW_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(bird_label, "C6")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY_COLOR),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            Create(bird_arrow),
            FadeIn(bird_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY_COLOR),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Flash the drone repeatedly
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(Flash(drone_asset, color=WHITE, flash_radius=0.4), run_time=0.5)
            self.wait(0.2)
            
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            'We usually define vectors using standard basis vectors.',
            'Vector i and vector j form our standard grid.',
            'Any vector is a combination of these basis vectors.',
            'Three steps along i and two along j.',
            'This gives us the coordinate pair three, two.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Standard Basis", lines)

        # Pre-define colors
        COLOR_I = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_J = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_GRID = "#555555"
        COLOR_V = "#FFFFFF"

        # Initialize Grid
        # We'll use a NumberPlane but position it within our grid area system
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_GRID, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": WHITE, "include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B2', 'E5')

        # Basis vectors defined via Arrows relative to plane coordinate system
        i_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=COLOR_I)
        j_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(0,1), buff=0, color=COLOR_J)
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency (FileNotFoundError: 'latex')
        i_label = Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_I, font_size=24).next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_J, font_size=24).next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Components for the example vector V = [3, 2]
        step_i = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(3,0), buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=2)
        step_j = Arrow(plane.c2p(3,0), plane.c2p(3,2), buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=2)
        vector_v = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(3,2), buff=0, color=COLOR_V)
        coords_label = Text("[3, 2]", color=COLOR_V, font_size=24).next_to(plane.c2p(3,2), UR, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_vec),
            GrowArrow(j_vec),
            Write(i_label),
            Write(j_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(step_i), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(step_j), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_v), Write(coords_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(step_i), FadeOut(step_j), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup current line color at the end
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introducing a New Basis", [
            'We can choose a different set of basis vectors.', 
            "Let's define new vectors b₁ and b₂.", 
            'These vectors form a tilted, non-perpendicular grid.', 
            'The same point has different coordinates in this system.', 
            'Each cell in this new grid is a parallelogram.'
        ])

        # Grid area constants
        grid_center = np.array([3.0, -0.3, 0])
        unit_scale = 0.7  # 1 unit in coordinate space = 0.7 Manim units

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Standard Grid (Gray)
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#555555", "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#555555", "stroke_width": 2}
        ).scale(unit_scale)
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Unit vectors i (#00FF00) and j (#0000FF)
        i_vec = Vector([unit_scale, 0], color="#00FF00")
        j_vec = Vector([0, unit_scale], color="#0000FF")
        i_vec.shift(grid_center)
        j_vec.shift(grid_center)
        
        # Labels using Text with unicode
        i_label = Text("î", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        j_label = Text("ĵ", color="#0000FF", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, "D5") 
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, "B3") 

        self.play(Create(std_grid), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), GrowArrow(j_vec), FadeIn(i_label), FadeIn(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # New basis vectors b1 = [2, 1] (#FF0000) and b2 = [-1, 1] (#FF8C00)
        b1_raw = np.array([2 * unit_scale, 1 * unit_scale, 0])
        b2_raw = np.array([-1 * unit_scale, 1 * unit_scale, 0])
        b1_vec = Vector(b1_raw, color="#FF0000").shift(grid_center)
        b2_vec = Vector(b2_raw, color="#FF8C00").shift(grid_center)
        
        b1_label = Text("b₁", color="#FF0000", font_size=20)
        b2_label = Text("b₂", color="#FF8C00", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(b1_label, "B5") 
        self.place_at_grid(b2_label, "B2") 

        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_vec), GrowArrow(b2_vec), FadeIn(b1_label), FadeIn(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        basis_matrix = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]
        
        tilted_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#FF0000", "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#FF0000", "stroke_opacity": 0.6}
        ).scale(unit_scale)
        tilted_grid.apply_matrix(basis_matrix)
        self.place_in_area(tilted_grid, "A1", "F6")

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(std_grid, tilted_grid),
            FadeOut(i_vec), FadeOut(j_vec), FadeOut(i_label), FadeOut(j_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Point (1, 2) in standard basis is (1, 1) in basis B
        dot_pos = grid_center + np.array([1 * unit_scale, 2 * unit_scale, 0])
        target_dot = Dot(dot_pos, color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.08)
        dot_label = Text("[1, 2]std", font_size=18, color=WHITE).next_to(target_dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(target_dot), Write(dot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Visualize a single basis parallelogram
        p_points = [
            grid_center,
            grid_center + b1_raw,
            grid_center + b1_raw + b2_raw,
            grid_center + b2_raw
        ]
        parallelogram = Polygon(*p_points, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=YELLOW, stroke_color=YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "The Change of Basis Matrix (The Bridge)"
        lines = [
            "Matrix P acts as a translator between coordinate systems.",
            "Its columns are the new basis vectors in standard coordinates.",
            "It bridges the gap between different perspectives."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_B1 = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_B2 = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        COLOR_STANDARD = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Create Coordinate System (Axes)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C}
        )
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        axes_label = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label=Text("x"), y_label=Text("y")).scale(0.6)
        axes_group = VGroup(axes, axes_label)
        self.place_in_area(axes_group, "C2", "F6")
        
        # Define vectors b1 and b2
        vec_b1 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(2, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        vec_b2 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        
        # Using Text for labels
        label_b1 = Text("b1", color=COLOR_STANDARD, font_size=24)
        label_b2 = Text("b2", color=COLOR_STANDARD, font_size=24)
        
        label_b1.next_to(vec_b1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_b2.next_to(vec_b2.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(vec_b1),
            Write(label_b1),
            GrowArrow(vec_b2),
            Write(label_b2),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_STANDARD)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Construct Matrix P manually using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        p_matrix_label = Text("P =", font_size=32)
        
        # Elements
        t2 = Text("2", font_size=28)
        t1_bot = Text("1", font_size=28)
        t_minus_1 = Text("-1", font_size=28)
        t1_top = Text("1", font_size=28)
        
        col1_vals = VGroup(t2, t1_bot).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        col2_vals = VGroup(t_minus_1, t1_top).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        matrix_elements = VGroup(col1_vals, col2_vals).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        
        # Manual brackets
        l_bracket = Text("[", font_size=48).scale([0.8, 1.8, 1]).next_to(matrix_elements, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        r_bracket = Text("]", font_size=48).scale([0.8, 1.8, 1]).next_to(matrix_elements, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        p_matrix = VGroup(l_bracket, matrix_elements, r_bracket)
        matrix_vgroup = VGroup(p_matrix_label, p_matrix).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_vgroup, "A1", "C4")
        
        self.play(Write(p_matrix_label), FadeIn(l_bracket), FadeIn(r_bracket))
        self.play(Write(col1_vals), Write(col2_vals), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_STANDARD)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        rect1 = SurroundingRectangle(col1_vals, color=COLOR_B1, buff=0.1)
        rect2 = SurroundingRectangle(col2_vals, color=COLOR_B2, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            vec_b1.animate.set_color(COLOR_B1),
            label_b1.animate.set_color(COLOR_B1),
            col1_vals.animate.set_color(COLOR_B1),
            Create(rect1),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            vec_b2.animate.set_color(COLOR_B2),
            label_b2.animate.set_color(COLOR_B2),

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    """
    Expert implementation of a Manim Scene focusing on layout management,
    grid-based positioning, and synchronized animations for Manim CE v0.19.0.
    """
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Configuration and Layout Setup
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        title_text = "Introduction to Manim Grid Systems"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Understanding Layouts",
            "- Defining Custom Grids",
            "- Placing Mobjects",
            "- Animating Sequences"
        ]

        # 2. UI Elements (Title and Lecture Notes)
        title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
        
        lecture_vgroup.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.0)

        # 3. Custom Grid System (Right-hand side visualization area)
        # Defining a coordinate mapping for precise object placement
        grid_map = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right
        
        # Grid bounds: X from 1 to 6, Y from 2 to -3
        start_x, start_y = 1.5, 2.0
        step = 1.0

        for i, row_label in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col_label in enumerate(cols):
                grid_map[f"{row_label}{col_label}"] = np.array([
                    start_x + (j * step), 
                    start_y - (i * step), 
                    0
                ])

        # 4. Mobjects Creation
        square = Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.4)
        circle = Circle(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.4)
        triangle = Triangle(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.4)

        # Positioning using grid system
        square.move_to(grid_map["A1"])
        circle.move_to(grid_map["C3"])
        triangle.move_to(grid_map["F6"])

        # 5. Animation Sequence
        # Sequence: Title -> Lecture -> Shapes
        self.play(Write(title), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(
                *[FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT) for line in lecture_vgroup],
                lag_ratio=0.3
            ),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(
            Create(square),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            GrowFromCenter(circle),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            SpinInFromNothing(triangle),
            run_time=1
        )

        # Final emphasis animation
        self.play(
            square.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(YELLOW),
            circle.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(ORANGE),
            triangle.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(PINK),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )

        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'First, identify your new set of basis vectors.',
            'Then, build matrix P to translate your coordinates.',
            'This logic powers rotations and perspectives in computer graphics.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visual Summary and Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lines
        COLOR_1 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        COLOR_2 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        COLOR_3 = "#00FF00" # Green
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_1)
        
        step1_text = Text("1. Identify Basis", font_size=24, color=COLOR_1)
        self.place_at_grid(step1_text, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Visual for basis vectors
        v1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=COLOR_1, buff=0)
        v2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP+RIGHT*0.5, color="#FF8800", buff=0)
        basis_group = VGroup(v1, v2)
        self.place_in_area(basis_group, "B2", "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(step1_text), Create(basis_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_2)
        
        step2_text = Text("2. Build Matrix P", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2)
        self.place_at_grid(step2_text, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        step3_text = Text("3. Multiply to translate", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2)
        self.place_at_grid(step3_text, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Visual for Matrix P
        p_label = Text("P = ", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2)
        m_elements = VGroup(
            Text("1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2), Text("0.5", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2),
            Text("0", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2), Text("1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2)
        ).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.4)
        l_bracket = Text("[", font_size=42, color=COLOR_2).next_to(m_elements, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        r_bracket = Text("]", font_size=42, color=COLOR_2).next_to(m_elements, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        matrix_p = VGroup(p_label, l_bracket, m_elements, r_bracket).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(matrix_p, "C4", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(step2_text), Write(step3_text), Write(matrix_p))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_3)
        
        # Clear previous visuals for the rotation demonstration
        self.play(FadeOut(basis_group), FadeOut(matrix_p), FadeOut(step1_text), FadeOut(step2_text), FadeOut(step3_text))
        
        # 2D Square rotating
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=COLOR_3, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(square, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Labels for the "Graphic Viewport"
        viewport_label = Text("Computer Graphics Logic", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(viewport_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(square), Write(viewport_label))
        
        # Continuous rotation using direct rotate
        self.play(Rotate(square, angle=2*PI, run_time=3, rate_func=linear))
        self.wait(1)

        # Final Transition
        # Fade to black
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(square), FadeOut(viewport_label))
        
        final_title = Text("Change of Basis: Different Lenses", font_size=42, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Write(final_title))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis: Viewing the World Through Different Lenses
outline.target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Concept of 'Perspective'
sections.content: Introduce the idea that the same physical point in space can be described by different sets of numbers depending on the 'ruler' or 'grid' we use. We use a relatable scenario where two characters perceive a location differently.
sections.example: A drone (Character A) flies in a grid aligned with the city streets, while a bird (Character B) perceives the world aligned with the direction of the wind (tilted 45 degrees). They both look at the same 'breadcomb' on the ground but describe its position using different coordinates.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Standard Basis
sections.content: Review the standard basis vectors i (1,0) and j (0,1). Explain that any vector [x, y] is actually a linear combination: x*i + y*j. Visualize a standard Cartesian grid with unit squares.
sections.example: Show a vector V = [3, 2] as 3 steps along the x-axis and 2 steps along the y-axis in a standard white-grid background.

sections.title: Introducing a New Basis
sections.content: Introduce a new set of basis vectors, B = {b1, b2}. These vectors are not necessarily perpendicular or unit length. Show a 'tilted' and 'stretched' grid over the original standard grid to illustrate a new coordinate system.
sections.example: Define b1 = [2, 1] and b2 = [-1, 1]. Draw these as red arrows on top of the standard blue grid. Show how they form their own 'tilted' coordinate system where each 'cell' is a parallelogram.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The Bridge)
sections.content: Explain how to construct the 'Change of Basis Matrix' (P). This matrix acts as a translator. The columns of P are simply the coordinates of the new basis vectors (b1 and b2) expressed in the language of the old (standard) basis.
sections.example: Construct Matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. Explain that the first column tells us where '1 unit' in the new system lands in the old system.

sections.title: The Transformation Formula
sections.content: Present the mathematical relationship: [v]_standard = P * [v]_new. Explain that multiplying a vector's 'new' coordinates by P transforms them back into the 'standard' coordinates. To go the other way (standard to new), we use the inverse matrix P^-1.
sections.example: If a squirrel thinks a nut is at [1, 1] in its 'tilted' B-basis, we calculate P * [1, 1] = [1, 2] to find where the nut is on our standard human grid.

sections.title: Visual Summary and Application
sections.content: Summarize the process: 1. Identify the new basis vectors. 2. Build the Matrix P. 3. Multiply to translate. Mention that this is how computer graphics tilt or rotate cameras (changing the basis of the viewport).
sections.example: Show a fast-motion animation of a 3D character rotating. Explain that the computer is constantly changing the 'basis' of the character's vertices to match the camera's perspective.

The drone follows a grid aligned with the streets.
The bird sees the world through a tilted grid.
Both observers point to the same physical location.
Same spot, but different coordinates based on their perspective.

storyboard.title: Introducing a New Basis
lecture_lines: We can choose an entirely different set of basis vectors.

They define a tilted and stretched coordinate grid.
A point at [1, 1] here means one of each.
We reach it by following the new basis vectors.

storyboard.title: The Transformation Formula
lecture_lines: This formula converts new coordinates back to standard ones.
Multiplying by P performs the translation between systems.
The result reveals the point's position in our standard grid.
Matrix P serves as the bridge between these perspectives.
Use P inverse to convert standard coordinates back to new.

Introduce the inverse formula [v]_new = P^-1 * [v]_std and highlight P^-1 in #FFD700.

Viewing the world through different lenses changes everything.
